key_insight: Grad Detect uses a single forward-backward pass to read layer-wise gradient patterns that reveal when an LLM is likely hallucinating, often more reliably than output confidence signals.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, interpretable way to add hallucination and abstention detection to deployed LLM systems with minimal extra inference cost and strong cross-model robustness.
method: Run one forward-backward pass at inference to collect layer-wise gradients.
Use the gradient structure as a predictor of hallucination or abstention.
Focus on the final layers, which contain most of the discriminative signal.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on several Q&A benchmarks across 11 models from four architectural families, Grad Detect consistently outperformed confidence-based and sampling-based baselines, with the final five layers carrying over 97% of the discriminative gradient signal.
watch_item: The approach still requires backward-pass computation at inference, so latency and memory overhead may limit use in very high-throughput or resource-constrained deployments.
paper_title: Grad Detect: Gradient-Based Hallucination Detection in LLMs
